name: Bloomberg

profile.reading: This is Bloombergs data center at 155 Corporate Drive in Orangeburg, in the Town of Orangetown, Rockland County, New York, about 25 miles north of New York City. The 143,331 square foot building was formerly owned by Verizon before being acquired by Russo Development Corporation in 2009, and Bloomberg does not own the building outright, per industry directory Baxtel. Bloomberg announced the project in May 2013 as a planned 710 million dollar investment over 15 years, including about 435 million dollars for initial renovation and equipment, after evaluating roughly 100 candidate sites across New York and New Jersey. Utility documents reviewed in coverage of the project describe up to 40 megawatts of provisioned electrical capacity available at the site through four 13 kilovolt circuits of 10 megawatts each, fed by subterranean 138 kilovolt ring bus transmission lines, though this figure represents capacity made available to the site rather than a confirmed fully built out IT load. The facility supports Bloomberg L.P.s trading and financial data infrastructure, with proximity to New York financial market connectivity hubs cited as a key site selection factor; Bloomberg is reported to operate at least two other data centers in the broader New York and New Jersey region as part of its East Coast infrastructure. Bloomberg L.P. is a privately held financial data, media, and software company founded in 1981 by Michael Bloomberg, who retains roughly 88 percent ownership, reporting about 15 billion dollars in revenue in 2024. Orangetown and the surrounding Rockland County area have attracted other large corporate back office and technology facilities over the years due to their position within reasonable commuting and network latency distance of Manhattan while offering lower real estate costs, a pattern common among financial sector technology infrastructure sited in the broader New York metropolitan region.
profile.research_note: Fresh research via Data Center Knowledge, Data Center Dynamics coverage of the May 2013 project announcement, and Baxtel. One tracker still showed a January 2024 permit application marked proposed for this address, so full completion status post-2013 announcement is not independently certain from sources checked, noted honestly.

reading:
Bloomberg L.P. is a privately held financial data and media company, and it is in this registry as an enterprise operator running a single data center for itself. The site is 155 Corporate Drive in Orangeburg, in the Town of Orangetown, Rockland County, New York, about 25 miles north of New York City. The building is a 143,331 square foot former Verizon property that Russo Development acquired in 2009 and redeveloped, and Bloomberg occupies it rather than owning it outright. Bloomberg announced the project in May 2013 as a 710 million dollar commitment over fifteen years, including about 435 million dollars for initial renovation and equipment, after evaluating roughly a hundred candidate sites across New York and New Jersey. Contemporary coverage put the build at around 250 construction jobs over eighteen months and about 80 permanent positions. The location logic was latency. The site sits roughly twelve miles from the NYSE Euronext matching engine facility in Mahwah, New Jersey.

Three power numbers circulate for this address and they are not the same thing. The developer's infrastructure material describes the property as able to take up to four 13 kV circuits and roughly 40 megawatts of utility service delivered underground from a nearby substation, which is service capacity, not load. The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation issued an Air State Facility permit for the site, identifier 3-3924-00434/00002, effective from January 2, 2024 to January 1, 2034, which describes the facility as a data processing center with up to eight emergency generators burning distillate oil. That is standby diesel. The permit is a synthetic minor, capping combined generator operation at 949 hours per year on a twelve month rolling basis expressly to stay under Title V major source thresholds, with a potential to emit of 49,500 pounds of nitrogen oxides per year, ultra low sulfur diesel at 0.0015 percent sulfur by weight and a 20 percent opacity limit on a six minute average. Bloomberg publishes no critical IT load for the building, and none is inferred here from either the utility service or the generators.

The local record around this facility has become active. Governor Kathy Hochul issued an executive order on July 14, 2026 pausing discretionary state permit applications for data centers capable of drawing at least 50 megawatts, for up to a year while the state completes an environmental review, leaving local zoning and building approvals untouched. In Rockland, where DataBank, 1547 Critical Systems and JPMorgan Chase also operate or are expanding, the Orangetown Town Board retained a planning consultant to study zoning changes and a possible local moratorium, with the town supervisor indicating that any local pause would not be applied retroactively.
